Contact.title: Contact
Contact.description: Represents a potential seller or lead in the Monica AI Hub, holding their personal, property, and engagement details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Contact entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the contact.

lastName.description: The last name of the contact.

email.description: The email address of the contact.

phone.description: The primary phone number of the contact.

addressStreet.description: The street address of the contact's mailing address.

addressCity.description: The city of the contact's mailing address.

addressState.description: The state or province of the contact's mailing address.

addressZipCode.description: The postal code of the contact's mailing address.

addressCountry.description: The country of the contact's mailing address.

propertyAddressStreet.description: The street address of the property the contact is selling or might sell.

propertyAddressCity.description: The city of the property the contact is selling or might sell.

propertyAddressState.description: The state or province of the property the contact is selling or might sell.

propertyAddressZipCode.description: The postal code of the property the contact is selling or might sell.

propertyAddressCountry.description: The country of the property the contact is selling or might sell.

status.description: The current engagement status of the contact (e.g., 'New', 'Engaged', 'Disqualified', 'Converted').

icpScore.description: An Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) score, indicating the contact's priority for outreach.

dncStatus.description: Indicates if the contact is on the Do Not Call (DNC) list.

lastContactedDate.description: Timestamp of the last time this contact was reached out to.

nextFollowUpDate.description: Timestamp for the planned next follow-up with this contact.

leadSourceId.description: Reference to the LeadSource entity from which this contact originated. (Relationship: LeadSource 1:N Contact)

sellerMotivation.description: Details about the seller's motivation for selling, used by AI for personalized outreach.

notes.description: General notes or additional information about the contact.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the contact record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the contact record was last updated.

LeadSource.title: LeadSource
LeadSource.description: Defines the origin of contact leads, such as ArchAgent, Vulcan7, or manual entry.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LeadSource entity.

name.description: The human-readable name of the lead source (e.g., 'ArchAgent', 'Vulcan7', 'Manual Entry', 'CSV Import').

type.description: The technical type of the lead source (e.g., 'Webhook', 'CSV', 'Manual', 'API').

description.description: A brief description of the lead source.

lastSyncTime.description: Timestamp of the last successful data synchronization from this lead source.

leadCount.description: The total number of leads imported from this source.

averageIcpScore.description: The average ICP score of contacts originating from this lead source.

LeadSourceConfiguration.title: LeadSourceConfiguration
LeadSourceConfiguration.description: Stores specific integration settings and preferences for each defined lead source.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LeadSourceConfiguration entity.

leadSourceId.description: Reference to the LeadSource entity this configuration applies to. (Relationship: LeadSource 1:1 LeadSourceConfiguration)

webhookUrl.description: The webhook URL for receiving lead data from the source (e.g., ArchAgent).

autoImportEnabled.description: Indicates if automatic lead import is enabled for this source.

dncSyncEnabled.description: Indicates if Do Not Call (DNC) list synchronization is enabled for this source (e.g., Vulcan7).

integrationMethod.description: The method of integration used for the lead source (e.g., 'Zapier', 'CSV Upload', 'Webhook').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the configuration was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the configuration was last updated.

CallLog.title: CallLog
CallLog.description: Records details of each AI-powered voice call made or received with a contact.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CallLog entity.

contactId.description: Reference to the Contact entity involved in the call. (Relationship: Contact 1:N CallLog)

durationSeconds.description: The duration of the call in seconds.

outcome.description: The result of the call (e.g., 'Connected', 'Voicemail', 'No Answer', 'DNC Request').

nextAction.description: A description of the next action planned after this call.

summary.description: An AI-generated summary of the call conversation.

callRecordingUrl.description: URL to the recording of the call, if available.

transcript.description: The full transcript of the call conversation.

aiInsights.description: AI-generated insights or sentiment analysis from the call, possibly in a JSON string format.

voicemailDropped.description: Indicates if an automated voicemail was dropped during the call.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the call log was created.

EmailLog.title: EmailLog
EmailLog.description: Records details of each personalized outreach email sent to a contact.

id.description: Unique identifier for the EmailLog entity.

contactId.description: Reference to the Contact entity who received the email. (Relationship: Contact 1:N EmailLog)

subject.description: The subject line of the email.

body.description: The full content of the email that was sent.

sentAt.description: Timestamp when the email was sent.

status.description: The delivery status of the email (e.g., 'Sent', 'Delivered', 'Opened', 'Bounced').

aiGenerated.description: Indicates if the email content was generated by AI.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the email log was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the email log was last updated.

SMSLog.title: SMSLog
SMSLog.description: Records details of each personalized SMS message sent to a contact.

id.description: Unique identifier for the SMSLog entity.

contactId.description: Reference to the Contact entity who received the SMS. (Relationship: Contact 1:N SMSLog)

message.description: The full content of the SMS message that was sent.

sentAt.description: Timestamp when the SMS was sent.

status.description: The delivery status of the SMS (e.g., 'Sent', 'Delivered', 'Failed').

aiGenerated.description: Indicates if the SMS content was generated by AI.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the SMS log was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the SMS log was last updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes strict user data segregation and authorization independence, adhering to the core design principles. All user-specific data is nested under a top-level `/users/{userId}/` collection. This path-based ownership (`/users/{userId}/contacts/{contactId}`, `/users/{userId}/leadSources/{leadSourceId}`, etc.) inherently ties all records to a specific authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`), making security rules simple and robust.

To achieve **Authorization Independence**, a critical mandate, every document across all collections will include a denormalized `ownerId` field, which will always match the `userId` in its path segment. For subcollections nested further (e.g., `callLogs` under `contacts`), the `contactId` will also be denormalized within the `CallLog`, `EmailLog`, and `SMSLog` documents. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore Security Rules to check parent document ownership or attributes, thus preventing rule complexity and allowing for atomic operations. For example, a `CallLog` document's access can be verified solely by checking `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId` and `request.path[3] == resource.data.ownerId` without needing to fetch the parent `contact` document.

**Querying for Authorized Paths (QAPs)** is fully supported by this structure. Because all user data resides under `/users/{userId}/`, a user's client-side queries for `contacts`, `leadSources`, `callLogs`, etc., will always be scoped by their `uid`. For example, `firestore.collection('users').doc(user.uid).collection('contacts')` will only retrieve contacts owned by `user.uid`. Security rules will simply enforce that `request.auth.uid` matches the `userId` wildcard in the path and the denormalized `ownerId` field, ensuring that unauthorized reads or writes are impossible. This structure eliminates the need for rules to act as filters, as the data a user can *access* is already structurally limited to their own. The consistent `ownerId` field also allows for more flexible querying patterns (e.g., aggregated dashboards that might query across contacts, but still need to filter by `ownerId` in a secure manner at the rule level, although direct `list` queries should primarily leverage the path structure for security). Structural segregation ensures homogeneous security posture within each collection, further simplifying rules.
